1000054.etyen:
Internationalism, from the European name tradition associated with the Gambia River and the territory surrounding it; compare English Gambia, the name used during British rule. The modern country takes its name from the river.
The river name is recorded in early European sources in several forms. The Venetian explorer Alvise Cadamosto, sailing in Portuguese service in 1455–1456, referred to the river as Gambra or Cambra; later forms included Gamba and Gambia. Portuguese navigators and traders were the first Europeans known to establish this naming tradition.

1004918.etyen:
From enke (“widow”) + hertuginne (“duchess”), literally “widow duchess”. The first element enke (“widow”) is from Old Danish ænkia (“widow”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *ainakjǭ (“widow”); the second element is hertuginne (“duchess”), from hertug (“duke”) + -inne (“feminine noun suffix”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish enkehertuginde, Swedish änkehertiginna and German Herzoginwitwe (“dowager duchess”).
